Private deployment considerations and KMS/HSM integration
header:
Date: 2025-04-07
Start: 16:00 PDT
Duration: 42 minutes
Attendees: Sofia Patel (Redwood AE), Marcus Nguyen (Redwood SE), Elena Gomez (Redwood Solutions), Dr. Elena Rivera (Acme CTO), Jake Morris (Acme Platform), Priya Singh (Acme Compliance), Tom Liao (Acme DevOps)
Recording: fireflies-export
Notes: product demo focused on data handling and retention controls
transcript:
[00:00] Sofia: Hey everyone, thanks for joining, this is Sofia from Redwood, I'll hand off to Marcus for a quick live demo focused on the privacy toggles.
[00:12] Dr. Elena: Hi Sofia, hi Marcus, quick note — we have to keep the meeting high level re: PHI examples, but we want to see the controls in action.
[00:18] Marcus: Totally, understood. I'll avoid raw PHI in samples. So agenda: Console walkthrough, API toggles, redaction rules, retention, then Q&A.
[00:29] Jake: Sounds good. We're especially interested in the ability to disable storage per-request and how redaction works for token logs.
[00:35] Marcus: Great — jumping into the Console now. (screen share) On the top nav you can see Projects -> Settings -> Data Controls. There's a store_requests toggle; default is on for hosted accounts but you can set it to off.
[00:50] Marcus: If you switch it off at the project level, new API calls will return with the metadata only, and request bodies are not persisted to our request-store. We also have per-route overrides.
[01:06] Priya: Is that immediate? Like, if we flip it will prior stored requests remain in the store?
[01:12] Marcus: Good question. The toggle affects persistence for incoming requests after the change. For historical data we have retention windows and you can trigger deletion/export. There's also a manual purge option but it requires an approval workflow.
[01:26] Sofia: And to add, for Dedicated/Private customers we support a mode where store_requests is effectively disabled because logs never leave the VPC unless you opt-in.
[01:36] Tom: For Private deployments, how does KMS work with redaction keys? We have an HSM requirement.
[01:42] Marcus: We integrate with customer-managed KMS for envelope encryption. For HSM-backed keys we have a KMS bridge that stores the key handle; Redwood never sees raw key material. That also ties into audit logs.
[01:55] Dr. Elena: Can you show API examples? Our SREs will likely script toggles.
[02:01] Marcus: Sure, here's the quick snippet — POST /v1/engines/{model}/completions with header X-Redwood-Project and query param store_requests=false. Example: curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/complete -H 'Authorization: Bearer <key>' -d '{"prompt":"[redacted]"}'?store_requests=false — actually the param is encoded as query or body depending on SDK. Our SDK exposes client.options.storeRequests = false.
[02:28] Jake: Any latency implications when store_requests is off? We rely on prefix caching so curious if there's a perf hit.
[02:35] Marcus: Minimal. The main difference is you skip writing to the request-store and any async auditing traces; write path is eliminated so often slightly faster, but you lose the ability to re-hydrate sessions from stored requests for debugging. Batching and KV cache path unaffected.
[02:51] Priya: On the redaction piece — does Redwood redact PII automatically or do we define patterns?
[02:58] Marcus: We have layers: first is an automated PII classifier that can flag tokens likely to be sensitive (names, SSNs, MRNs). Second, you can define redaction policies — regexes, named-entity rules, and custom field masks. Third, there's an explicit redaction API where you submit a request id and it will sanitize stored artifacts.
[03:16] Sofia: Note: the automated classifier is configurable with sensitivity levels — conservative, default, aggressive. You can preview what would be redacted in the Console before applying.
[03:28] (brief screen flicker)
[03:30] Marcus: Showing the Preview tab: you upload a sample prompt and it highlights tokens we'd redact. The preview shows both automatic classifier hits and policy-based matches.
[03:41] Dr. Elena: Can we keep some meta fields but redact content? E.g., store usage metrics and token counts for billing but not prompt text.
[03:49] Marcus: Yes — we split telemetry. You can enable storing derived metadata like token_count, latency, status while turning off storing raw prompt/response. That's the store_metadata_only profile.
[03:58] Jake: What about audit trails for compliance — we need to show a chain of custody without exposing content.
[04:05] Marcus: We support audit logs that record the event (request received, processed, redaction applied) with stable identifiers and hashes — we store a SHA256 hash of the prompt if you need content verification without seeing plaintext. Hashing is optional and can be keyed with your KMS so only you can map back.
[04:22] Priya: That sounds useful. Is the hashed value sufficient for regulators? We'd have to discuss with legal.
[04:27] Sofia: We find customers often pair the hashed-record approach with a small allowed retention window for plaintext in a sealed store — e.g., 7 days — to enable troubleshooting, then automatically purge.
[04:36] Marcus: Switching to retention settings: you can set retention at project, route, or API-key levels. Options are immediate purge, 1d, 7d, 30d, 90d, or custom up to x years for Dedicated contracts.
[04:50] Tom: Is deletion immediate or eventually consistent?
[04:54] Marcus: Deletions are eventual but typically completed within minutes; for Private on-prem we can do synchronous zero-keep deletes if required.
[05:03] Dr. Elena: How are deletions verified? We need attestations.
[05:06] Marcus: We provide deletion receipts — signed events with timestamp and deletion id. For high-assurance customers we can export the audit trail signed with your KMS.
[05:16] (two people speaking briefly, inaudible)
[05:20] Priya: About redaction accuracy — does the classifier ever false-positive names from clinical text?
[05:26] Marcus: Yes, clinical jargon can cause false positives; the Console preview helps tune rules. We also support uploading labeled examples to fine-tune classifier thresholds per project.
[05:37] Sophia: (correcting) Sofia: we also have a 'safe examples' flag so you can whitelist tokens or fields that should never be redacted.
[05:45] Jake: How does this tie into Redwood Optimize — like can Optimize recommend a quantization or batching profile while we keep store_requests off?
[05:52] Marcus: Redwood Optimize is orthogonal — it analyzes token patterns and suggests batching/cache sizes and model variants. It only needs metadata; you can run Optimize with store_metadata_only to get suggestions without storing raw prompts.
[06:06] Dr. Elena: Good. We also want to integrate logs with our Splunk / Datadog. What's the integration story?
[06:12] Marcus: We export structured events to your logging endpoint via webhooks or push connectors. You can choose to send full payloads, metadata-only, or hashed references. We also support S3 export for bulk archives.
[06:23] Priya: For legal discovery, sometimes we need to retain certain transcripts longer — can we have retention exceptions per conversation?
[06:29] Marcus: Yes, you can set hold policies on specific request IDs or routes; holds keep data until manually released and are recorded in the audit log with approver metadata.
[06:38] (short pause)
[06:40] Tom: Any gotchas on the SDK side? For example, does node SDK always send a copy of the prompt in debug logs?
[06:46] Marcus: SDKs have a debug flag — by default debug logs are off in production builds. When enabled they may log full prompt locally, but not send extra telemetry to Redwood unless you explicitly set client.options.debugUpload = true. We caution against enabling debug in production.
[07:02] Sofia: Quick demo of API change rollback — if a new route defaulted to store_requests=true we recommend canarying and then flipping to false. Console supports route-level rollouts with percentage based traffic splits.
[07:16] Dr. Elena: We need an approval workflow for toggles, not just a flip. Can Redwood integrate with our SSO and RBAC?
[07:23] Marcus: Yes — SSO via SAML/Okta is supported. RBAC roles map to Console UI privileges, and toggle changes can require multi-approver sign-off which we record in the audit logs.
[07:35] Priya: What about encryption at rest and in transit?
[07:39] Marcus: TLS everywhere in transit. At rest we use AES-256; for Dedicated/Private we support CMK (customer-managed keys) and integrate with HSM-backed KMS.
[07:49] Jake: Can you demo the redaction rule UI and show how a custom regex is validated?
[07:54] Marcus: Sure. (still sharing) In the policies tab you can add a new rule, choose type regex, test against sample text inline. It highlights matches and shows a brief performance estimate — complex regexes can add CPU overhead on ingestion, we flag that.
[08:12] Dr. Elena: We might have thousands of messages per day, performance matters.
[08:16] Marcus: For high-throughput routes we recommend moving heavy rules to offline post-processing or using the classifier-only fast path. Also batching reduces cost.
[08:27] Sofia: Are there pre-built HIPAA templates?
[08:29] Marcus: Yes — there's a HIPAA compliance template that sets conservative classifier sensitivity, 7-day retention, required approvers, and KMS integration checklists. You can clone it and tweak.
[08:41] Priya: Will we get a mapping of Redwood controls to our HITRUST/HIPAA controls?
[08:45] Sofia: We'll send a compliance mapping doc — that will be in the security pack.
[08:50] (brief crosstalk)
[08:54] Marcus: Quick QA: here's an example of the redaction REST call — POST /v1/requests/{id}/redact with body {"rules":["mask-ssn","mask-name"], "dry_run": true}. Dry run returns diff. After you review you call same endpoint with dry_run=false.
[09:12] Jake: Nice. On the billing side — if we disable storage do we still get charged for those tokens?
[09:18] Sofia: Yes, billing is token-based. Storage toggles affect storage and audit charges but not inference compute/token charges.
[09:26] Tom: For Private infra, can the audit logs be forwarded to our SIEM without Redwood seeing content?
[09:32] Marcus: Yes, use the export connector with hashed references or metadata only; the export can be configured to strip body content before leaving the VPC.
[09:41] Priya: Are there SOC2 attestation docs for these flows?
[09:44] Sofia: Yes, included in the pack. We'll include details of the retention/deletion receipts.
[09:50] Marcus: Now moving to an edge-case: cross-region replication. If you have global traffic and store_requests is off in one region but on in another, we follow region-level policy; requests are persisted where they land. We recommend setting global project default.
[10:06] Dr. Elena: Behaviour sounds predictable — if we run a pilot can you provide a short support SLA?
[10:11] Sofia: For pilots we usually offer a 24h support response and weekday engineering office hours. For Dedicated SLAs we have higher guarantees.
[10:19] (screen show changes page)
[10:22] Marcus: Demoing programmatic toggle via Terraform provider — you can manage redwood_data_controls resource with fields: store_requests, retention_days, redaction_policy_id.
[10:34] Jake: Excellent — we'll prefer IaC for reproducibility.
[10:37] Mate: (mislabelled, faint)
[10:40] Marcus: Sorry, small typo on the resource name; we'll share exact Terraform examples.
[10:46] Dr. Elena: One more question on incident response — if there's an exfil attempt how fast can we revoke keys and isolate logged requests?
[10:53] Marcus: You can rotate API keys immediately, flip project-level store_requests to false, and initiate a forensic purge. For Dedicated we can snapshot and hand over encrypted archives for your IR team.
[11:07] Priya: Do you have a defined breach notification timeline?
[11:10] Sofia: Yes, it's in the contract addendum — standard is 72 hours for confirmed incidents and we coordinate with your security lead.
[11:18] (people typing)
[11:22] Marcus: Wrapping up — recommended pilot config: project-level store_requests=false, store_metadata_only enabled, classifier sensitivity conservative, retention 7d with hashed verification and manual purge workflow.
[11:36] Dr. Elena: That aligns with our risk appetite. We'll confirm internal stakeholders.
[11:42] Sofia: Next steps recap: we'll send security pack, Terraform and SDK snippets, and a short how-to video. Marcus will own the video.
[11:52] Jake: Thanks, one ask — can you include a sample audit deletion receipt?
[11:57] Sofia: Yes, included in the security pack.
[12:00] (wrap-up, small chatter)
[12:05] Marcus: Thanks everyone, we'll post recording and notes.
[12:10] Dr. Elena: Appreciate it, talk soon.
[12:16] (call ends)

Notes on transcription: occasional word swaps and small mislabels (e.g., "Mate" briefly appears), some timestamps approximate.
